findings.claim: The test comment and commit message say a main that is not ahead is still not pushed, but TestApplyPushStepKeepsItsOtherBehaviour only covers the no-origin case. No origin with a non-ahead main is ever configured, so that behaviour has no test. The trailing os.Stat check on work/.git only confirms the fixture was created and asserts nothing about the step.

The classifier treats any host:path or scheme:// URL as a network remote. A loopback or same-machine ssh origin such as localhost:/repo or ssh://localhost/repo would still receive the push, so the scratch-clone protection covers only path-style origins. A user whose real origin is a local bare path now silently stops publishing main, and only an info line records it.

evidence: Read the case patterns in origin_is_network_remote: empty, file://, absolute, ./, ../, ~ and Windows drive paths return 1; scheme:// returns 0; host:path returns 0 only when the part before the first colon contains no slash. This matches the stated intent.
The extracted push_main_to_origin keeps the no-origin and ahead-count logic unchanged, and cmd_apply still returns 1 when an mcp install failed or a pi stub was included.
The first new test mocks git push, so none of the seven URL cases can reach a real remote.
